blocks.text: Dohra:

There lived a (devout) Singh named Subeg Singh Jambhar1 , Who was a staunch follower of Sikh ideology and its tenets. Even he was a devout Sikh of the Sikh Gurus, Who had begot Subeg Singh Jambar. (1)
lines: There lived a (devout) Singh named Subeg Singh Jambhar1 ,
Who was a staunch follower of Sikh ideology and its tenets.
Even he was a devout Sikh of the Sikh Gurus,
Who had begot Subeg Singh Jambar.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Educating his son in the Persian language in childhood, His father got him employed in the Mughal court. He, being a supplier of provisions to the Mughals on contract, He had his residence in the (central) city of Lahore. (2)
lines: Educating his son in the Persian language in childhood,
His father got him employed in the Mughal court.
He, being a supplier of provisions to the Mughals on contract,
He had his residence in the (central) city of Lahore.

blocks.text: The Mughals would, often, send him as their emissary to the Khalsa, As the Khalsa Panth, too, had a good opinion about him. Whenever the Mughals had any pressing issue to be sorted out, They would make him their emissary with many solicitations. (3)
lines: The Mughals would, often, send him as their emissary to the Khalsa,
As the Khalsa Panth, too, had a good opinion about him.
Whenever the Mughals had any pressing issue to be sorted out,
They would make him their emissary with many solicitations.

blocks.text: As he had gone (on diplomatic missions) to the Singhs many a time, The Singhs, too, wished to remain on good terms with him. His services would the Mughals utilize through various tactics, Sometime through state pressure, force or else solicitation and manipulation. (4)
lines: As he had gone (on diplomatic missions) to the Singhs many a time,
The Singhs, too, wished to remain on good terms with him.
His services would the Mughals utilize through various tactics,
Sometime through state pressure, force or else solicitation and manipulation.

blocks.text: All state secrets would he reveal to the Khalsa Singhs, He, being a great well-wisher of the Khalsa Panth. He could sacrifice all that he possessed for the Khalsa Panth, Even at the cost of severing his closest family ties. (5)
lines: All state secrets would he reveal to the Khalsa Singhs,
He, being a great well-wisher of the Khalsa Panth.
He could sacrifice all that he possessed for the Khalsa Panth,
Even at the cost of severing his closest family ties.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Such a human being was Subeg Singh Jambar, A man of ascetic, meditative and resolute disposition. (Dear readers), the author beseeches you to listen with concentration, The way the (wicked) Mughals dealth with such a pious man. (6)
lines: Such a human being was Subeg Singh Jambar,
A man of ascetic, meditative and resolute disposition.
(Dear readers), the author beseeches you to listen with concentration,
The way the (wicked) Mughals dealth with such a pious man.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Taking Subeg Singh into custody from his village Jambar, The Mughals captured his infant son along with him. Offering various temptations of money, employment and landed property, The Lahore Nawab asked him to get converted to Islam. (7)
lines: Taking Subeg Singh into custody from his village Jambar,
The Mughals captured his infant son along with him.
Offering various temptations of money, employment and landed property,
The Lahore Nawab asked him to get converted to Islam.

blocks.text: Otherwise Subeg Singh should get prepared to die, With his body being crushed between the wheels with spokes. At this, lowing his head in acceptance, Subeg Singh remarked, Blessed be that instrument and the moment (when he dies for his faith). (8)
lines: Otherwise Subeg Singh should get prepared to die,
With his body being crushed between the wheels with spokes.
At this, lowing his head in acceptance,
Subeg Singh remarked,
Blessed be that instrument and the moment (when he dies for his faith).

blocks.text: He begged the Nawab to put him on the torture rack, And have done with him without any further loss of time. As he had been a devout Sikh of the great Gurus, He would feel blessed to shed his mortal frame for his faith. (9)
lines: He begged the Nawab to put him on the torture rack,
And have done with him without any further loss of time.
As he had been a devout Sikh of the great Gurus,
He would feel blessed to shed his mortal frame for his faith.

blocks.text: Great was the Nawab, greater still was his faith in Islam, Great must be his sense of justice, he being a legal expert. Should he (Subeg Singh) convert to Islam for fear of death, Would he never die after his conversion to Islam? (10)
lines: Great was the Nawab, greater still was his faith in Islam,
Great must be his sense of justice, he being a legal expert.
Should he (Subeg Singh) convert to Islam for fear of death,
Would he never die after his conversion to Islam?

blocks.text: If death is imminent even after getting converted, Why should he give up his own religion in this life? He would gladly convert to Islam to escape death, Provided Islam guaranteed that he would never die. (11)
lines: If death is imminent even after getting converted,
Why should he give up his own religion in this life?
He would gladly convert to Islam to escape death,
Provided Islam guaranteed that he would never die.

blocks.text: As Islam was very dear to the worthy Nawab, So was his (Subeg Singh's) own religion very dear to him. He pleaded to be immediately executed on the torture rack, And be done away with without any further loss of time. (12)
lines: As Islam was very dear to the worthy Nawab,
So was his (Subeg Singh's) own religion very dear to him.
He pleaded to be immediately executed on the torture rack,
And be done away with without any further loss of time.

blocks.text: Firmly refusing to be got converted to Islam, He reiterated his resolve to sacrifice his life for his faith. Thereafter, issuing the orders for his execution, Subeg Singh's body was fixed between the wheels with spokes. (13)
lines: Firmly refusing to be got converted to Islam,
He reiterated his resolve to sacrifice his life for his faith.
Thereafter, issuing the orders for his execution,
Subeg Singh's body was fixed between the wheels with spokes.

blocks.text: As the two wheels, with his body in between, were put into motion, Subeg Singh did not forget to meditate on God's name. As he kept on repeating the name of the Divine Guru, He also shouted the Singh slogan of victory Akal! Akal. (14)
lines: As the two wheels, with his body in between, were put into motion,
Subeg Singh did not forget to meditate on God's name.
As he kept on repeating the name of the Divine Guru,
He also shouted the Singh slogan of victory Akal!
Akal.

blocks.text: Feeling more infuriated after hearing these Singh slogans, He ordered to move the wheels more speedily to silence the Singh's voice. The faster the wheels moved, the louder became the Singh's slogans, As he did not lose his faith in the sacred name of Guru Nanak. (15)
lines: Feeling more infuriated after hearing these Singh slogans,
He ordered to move the wheels more speedily to silence the Singh's voice.
The faster the wheels moved, the louder became the Singh's slogans,
As he did not lose his faith in the sacred name of Guru Nanak.

blocks.text: Dohra:

(Failing to subdue his spirits), the Nawab issued fresh orders, That Subeg Singh's body be unhinged from the torture rack. He ordered Subeg's son to be put on the same device, So that Subeg Singh might witness his infant son's torture. (16)
lines: (Failing to subdue his spirits), the Nawab issued fresh orders,
That Subeg Singh's body be unhinged from the torture rack.
He ordered Subeg's son to be put on the same device,
So that Subeg Singh might witness his infant son's torture.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The executioners, carrying on the orders of the Nawab, Hung the infants' body upside down with his legs tied. As they moved the spoked wheels with full force, Subeg Singh was made to see the torture with his own eyes. (17)
lines: The executioners, carrying on the orders of the Nawab,
Hung the infants' body upside down with his legs tied.
As they moved the spoked wheels with full force,
Subeg Singh was made to see the torture with his own eyes.

blocks.text: Overwhelmed with emotion, Subeg Singh kept remarking, Blessed be his son and blessed be the day of sacrifice. Blessed be the person who died for his faith, Blessed be he who yearned for the lotus feet of the Guru. (18)
lines: Overwhelmed with emotion,
Subeg Singh kept remarking,
Blessed be his son and blessed be the day of sacrifice.
Blessed be the person who died for his faith,
Blessed be he who yearned for the lotus feet of the Guru.

blocks.text: Thereafter bringing the child down after so much torture, The Nawab tried to bring him round through these mortifications. Telling the child that he, being immature, lacked wisdom, Why should he lose his life by being obdurate? (19)
lines: Thereafter bringing the child down after so much torture,
The Nawab tried to bring him round through these mortifications.
Telling the child that he, being immature, lacked wisdom,
Why should he lose his life by being obdurate?

blocks.text: Informing the child that while his father had enjoyed every joy of life, Why should he deprive himself of good days ahead? What good purpose would it serve to keep his faith, If he ended his life without enjoying the comforts of life? (20)
lines: Informing the child that while his father had enjoyed every joy of life,
Why should he deprive himself of good days ahead?
What good purpose would it serve to keep his faith,
If he ended his life without enjoying the comforts of life?

blocks.text: Dohra:

Impressing upon the child to get converted to Islam, The Nawab offered to grant him a vast landed property. So long as the country remained under a sovereign rule, Nobody could deprive him of his possession of that property. (21)
lines: Impressing upon the child to get converted to Islam,
The Nawab offered to grant him a vast landed property.
So long as the country remained under a sovereign rule,
Nobody could deprive him of his possession of that property.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Addressing Subeg Singh once again, remarked the Nawab, That he should save his son's life from the executioner's sword. He should keep his family line alive by saving his son, By swearing on the Islam's Koranic religious verses. (22)
lines: Addressing Subeg Singh once again, remarked the Nawab,
That he should save his son's life from the executioner's sword.
He should keep his family line alive by saving his son,
By swearing on the Islam's Koranic religious verses.

blocks.text: The Nawab threatened to slaughter together with village populace, Otherwise he should instruct his son to convert to Islam. As his own life would also be spared after his son's conversion, Subeg Singh should show some concern for his son's life. (23)
lines: The Nawab threatened to slaughter together with village populace,
Otherwise he should instruct his son to convert to Islam.
As his own life would also be spared after his son's conversion,
Subeg Singh should show some concern for his son's life.

blocks.text: Survival of sons alone keeps a family line going, As families without sons are rendered issueless. Hearing this advice Subeg Singh said to the Nawab, That the latter was, indeed, speaking the truth. (24)
lines: Survival of sons alone keeps a family line going,
As families without sons are rendered issueless.
Hearing this advice Subeg Singh said to the Nawab,
That the latter was, indeed, speaking the truth.

blocks.text: Since he (Subeg Singh) had earned his livelihood from Nawab's service, It did not behove him to use unparliamentary words before his boss. He would tender only one advice to his son, That the great Guru alone was the preserver of a Sikh's life. (25)
lines: Since he (Subeg Singh) had earned his livelihood from Nawab's service,
It did not behove him to use unparliamentary words before his boss.
He would tender only one advice to his son,
That the great Guru alone was the preserver of a Sikh's life.

blocks.text: While there existed hardly any certainty about life, Inevitability of death was an accepted universal norm. So let our faith abide, though we be dead in body soon, How long could man survive after giving up one's faith. (26)
lines: While there existed hardly any certainty about life,
Inevitability of death was an accepted universal norm.
So let our faith abide, though we be dead in body soon,
How long could man survive after giving up one's faith.

blocks.text: Why should one give up one's faith for a temporal life, How could man escape death as it is inevitable. The Sikh Gurus had served the cause of Khalsa Panth, Even as they sacrificed their lives together with their progeny. (27)
lines: Why should one give up one's faith for a temporal life,
How could man escape death as it is inevitable.
The Sikh Gurus had served the cause of Khalsa Panth,
Even as they sacrificed their lives together with their progeny.

blocks.text: All the four sons of the Guru had given up their life, Sacrificing their lives at the altar of goddess of war. As they had sacrificed their whole family for the sake of the Sikhs, What distinction would the Sikhs earn preserving their progeny? (28)
lines: All the four sons of the Guru had given up their life,
Sacrificing their lives at the altar of goddess of war.
As they had sacrificed their whole family for the sake of the Sikhs,
What distinction would the Sikhs earn preserving their progeny?

blocks.text: As this dialogue continued for some time, The Nawab had different thoughts in his mind. As the kind of advice Subeg Singh was tendering his son, The child was getting more and more adamant in his conviction. (29)
lines: As this dialogue continued for some time,
The Nawab had different thoughts in his mind.
As the kind of advice Subeg Singh was tendering his son,
The child was getting more and more adamant in his conviction.

blocks.text: He thought he must separate the son from his father, And convert him to Islam through duress and threats. As the child's body would writhe in excruciating pain, He would forget everything about his Guru and guide. (30)
lines: He thought he must separate the son from his father,
And convert him to Islam through duress and threats.
As the child's body would writhe in excruciating pain,
He would forget everything about his Guru and guide.

blocks.text: The Nawab ordered to subject the child to extreme tortures, As well as grant land gifts if the child so desired. Thereafter, the executioners began to torture the child severely, With dragging him from his feet and giving blows on his face. (31)
lines: The Nawab ordered to subject the child to extreme tortures,
As well as grant land gifts if the child so desired.
Thereafter, the executioners began to torture the child severely,
With dragging him from his feet and giving blows on his face.

blocks.text: Revolving his whole body by dangling it from a single leg, They would then throw him back by pulling his arm. Pricking his body with the their sharp teeth and nails, They would mortify him through several twists and turns. (32)
lines: Revolving his whole body by dangling it from a single leg,
They would then throw him back by pulling his arm.
Pricking his body with the their sharp teeth and nails,
They would mortify him through several twists and turns.

blocks.text: Inflicting pain by pulling at his nose and ears, They would threaten him with knocking down his teeth. Somebody remarked that the child was pretending to be unconscious, He must be skinned alive for his feigning unconsciousness. (33)
lines: Inflicting pain by pulling at his nose and ears,
They would threaten him with knocking down his teeth.
Somebody remarked that the child was pretending to be unconscious,
He must be skinned alive for his feigning unconsciousness.

blocks.text: My (author's) tongue fails to narrate the mortifications, Which were inflicted (on the tender body of this child). Instructing the executioners to fit him between the spoked wheels again, The Nawab ordered them to keep torturing him till he died. (34)
lines: My (author's) tongue fails to narrate the mortifications,
Which were inflicted (on the tender body of this child).
Instructing the executioners to fit him between the spoked wheels again,
The Nawab ordered them to keep torturing him till he died.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the executioners got exhausted with their job, Exhausting all means of torturing a human body, The child also went into a spell of deep silence, As a fit of spasmodic convulsion hit his system. (35)
lines: As the executioners got exhausted with their job,
Exhausting all means of torturing a human body,
The child also went into a spell of deep silence,
As a fit of spasmodic convulsion hit his system.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
At this, the executioner gave an indication, That the child was on the verge of death. Subeg Singh felt elated at this remark, As the revered Guru had upheld his self-respect. (36)
lines: At this, the executioner gave an indication,
That the child was on the verge of death.
Subeg Singh felt elated at this remark,
As the revered Guru had upheld his self-respect.

blocks.text: Blessed be his son and blessed be the womb who begot him, As their faith had been vindicated through their noble deeds. Subeg Singh recalled another similar incident (of religious conviction), Where a father had voluntarily got his son sawn into two pieces. (37)
lines: Blessed be his son and blessed be the womb who begot him,
As their faith had been vindicated through their noble deeds.
Subeg Singh recalled another similar incident (of religious conviction),
Where a father had voluntarily got his son sawn into two pieces.

blocks.text: Thereafter ordering a servant to fetch some water, The Nawab, after sprinkling a bit on the child's face, put it in his mouth. As the child regained a bit of consciousness, The Nawab patted him to bolster his self-confidence. (38)
lines: Thereafter ordering a servant to fetch some water,
The Nawab, after sprinkling a bit on the child's face, put it in his mouth.
As the child regained a bit of consciousness,
The Nawab patted him to bolster his self-confidence.

blocks.text: Telling the child that since he had been born again after regaining consciousness, He would not be accused of converting to Islam after a new life. Summoning all the Hindus who had converted to Islam, He made them stand by the side of the child. (39)
lines: Telling the child that since he had been born again after regaining consciousness,
He would not be accused of converting to Islam after a new life.
Summoning all the Hindus who had converted to Islam,
He made them stand by the side of the child.

blocks.text: Persuading the child through their glib talk, These converts prompted him to say he would convert to Islam. Drifting between spells of unconsciousness and awakening, He spoke a few words with a staggering tongue.(40)
lines: Persuading the child through their glib talk,
These converts prompted him to say he would convert to Islam.
Drifting between spells of unconsciousness and awakening,
He spoke a few words with a staggering tongue.

blocks.text: The Nawab heaved a sigh of great relief, As he made the child say, "I would convert to Islam". "The child has been misled to convert through threats of torture", Subeg Singh heard his own words reverberating into his ears. (41)
lines: The Nawab heaved a sigh of great relief,
As he made the child say,
"I would convert to Islam".
"The child has been misled to convert through threats of torture",
Subeg Singh heard his own words reverberating into his ears.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Being bewildered (at this sudden turn of events), Subeg Singh felt extremely pained at heart. Summoning the child to where Subeg Singh stood, The Nawab remarked that the child was converting to Islam.
Chaupai:

To Subeg Singh's query : What made him think of converting to Islam? The child replied that he could no longer bear the torture. Hearing this, Subeg Singh was stunned into dumb-foundedness, As he felt extremely desperate at such a catastrophe. (43)
lines: To Subeg Singh's query : What made him think of converting to Islam?
The child replied that he could no longer bear the torture.
Hearing this,
Subeg Singh was stunned into dumb-foundedness,
As he felt extremely desperate at such a catastrophe.

blocks.text: Soon after it occurred into Subeg Singh's mind, That he should have a look at his son's face. He must examine how he was going to recite the Koranic verse, And why was he willing to forget the Guru's Name. (44)
lines: Soon after it occurred into Subeg Singh's mind,
That he should have a look at his son's face.
He must examine how he was going to recite the Koranic verse,
And why was he willing to forget the Guru's Name.

blocks.text: Calling his son to him from where he stood with the Nawab, Subeg Singh attempted to persuade him gently. "Dear Son, what made you forget the Satguru's Name, Had anyone threatened you with a sword?" (45)
lines: Calling his son to him from where he stood with the Nawab,
Subeg Singh attempted to persuade him gently.
"Dear Son, what made you forget the Satguru's Name,
Had anyone threatened you with a sword?"

blocks.text: Dohra:

As Subeg Singh looked at the child's forehead closely, He found that the child was destined to be converted. Shaking his head in desperation after deciphering the inscription, He expressed deep regret at his son's destined misfortune. (46)
lines: As Subeg Singh looked at the child's forehead closely,
He found that the child was destined to be converted.
Shaking his head in desperation after deciphering the inscription,
He expressed deep regret at his son's destined misfortune.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As Subeg Singh had deciphered from the child's forehead, His son was destined to be converted to Islam. Thereafter removing a shoe from one of his own feet, He touched the child's forehead with his bare foot. (47)
lines: As Subeg Singh had deciphered from the child's forehead,
His son was destined to be converted to Islam.
Thereafter removing a shoe from one of his own feet,
He touched the child's forehead with his bare foot.

blocks.text: Reciting the divine slogan Akal! Akal! loudly, The pious Khalsa (Subeg Singh) effaced the blasphemous inscription. With the chanting of the sacred name of the Divine creator, The predestined inscription was totally effaced. (48)
lines: Reciting the divine slogan Akal!
Akal! loudly,
The pious Khalsa (Subeg Singh) effaced the blasphemous inscription.
With the chanting of the sacred name of the Divine creator,
The predestined inscription was totally effaced.

blocks.text: It became an occurring well-known in the world, That the word "Khalsa" came to be inscribed on the child's forehead. As a saint, if he wills, could as much efface a person's destined lot, As he could alter altogether the predestined fortune. (49)
lines: It became an occurring well-known in the world,
That the word "Khalsa" came to be inscribed on the child's forehead.
As a saint, if he wills, could as much efface a person's destined lot,
As he could alter altogether the predestined fortune.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Nawab looked at (Subeg Singh's strange gesture), He felt a bit disturbed in his own mind. Questioning Subeg Singh's touching child's head with his barefoot, The Nawab asked him to explain the implications of his act. (50)
lines: As the Nawab looked at (Subeg Singh's strange gesture),
He felt a bit disturbed in his own mind.
Questioning Subeg Singh's touching child's head with his barefoot,
The Nawab asked him to explain the implications of his act.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

To Nawab 's query, replied Subeg Singh in this vein, That the latter had effaced the child's predestined fortune. As the Nawab declared it to be a white lie, Subeg Singh asked the Nawab to confirm it from the child. (51)
lines: To Nawab 's query, replied Subeg Singh in this vein,
That the latter had effaced the child's predestined fortune.
As the Nawab declared it to be a white lie,
Subeg Singh asked the Nawab to confirm it from the child.

blocks.text: As the Nawab started questioning the child, The child turned a deaf ear to all his queries. Asking the child to get converted to Islam, He promisted to spare his life after his conversion. (52)
lines: As the Nawab started questioning the child,
The child turned a deaf ear to all his queries.
Asking the child to get converted to Islam,
He promisted to spare his life after his conversion.

blocks.text: At this child told the Nawab (in unmistakable terms), That his own faith's teachings were dear to him. As he (the child) had received God's true Name from his Guru, The Guru had blessed him with the Divine name "Waheguru". (53)
lines: At this child told the Nawab (in unmistakable terms),
That his own faith's teachings were dear to him.
As he (the child) had received God's true Name from his Guru,
The Guru had blessed him with the Divine name "Waheguru".

blocks.text: Getting infuriated at the child's curt, bold reply, The Nawab ordered the child to be tortured severely. After this, even when the child was tortured far more severely, The child felt comforted at his chastisement. (54)
lines: Getting infuriated at the child's curt, bold reply,
The Nawab ordered the child to be tortured severely.
After this, even when the child was tortured far more severely,
The child felt comforted at his chastisement.

blocks.text: As the saintly child Prehlad2 had not experienced pain, Subeg Singh's son, too, derived comfort from his torture. The more the child was beaten and thrashed, The more the child rejoiced at his persecution. (55)
lines: As the saintly child Prehlad2 had not experienced pain,
Subeg Singh's son, too, derived comfort from his torture.
The more the child was beaten and thrashed,
The more the child rejoiced at his persecution.

blocks.text: The executioners got exhausted with mortifying the child, As they had exhausted all means of persecuting him. At this, it occurred to the Nawab's (disturbed) mind, That some kind of a magic spell had been cast on the child.(56)
lines: The executioners got exhausted with mortifying the child,
As they had exhausted all means of persecuting him.
At this, it occurred to the Nawab's (disturbed) mind,
That some kind of a magic spell had been cast on the child.

blocks.text: Summoning the Muslim clerics and Islamic theologians, He asked them to neutralize the alleged magic spell. Asking them to try their best through the Koranic incantations, They must get the child converted to Islam. (57)
lines: Summoning the Muslim clerics and Islamic theologians,
He asked them to neutralize the alleged magic spell.
Asking them to try their best through the Koranic incantations,
They must get the child converted to Islam.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Having recited all the Koranic incantations, The clerics failed to get the child converted. As the true Khalsa (Subeg Singh's son) remained completely unaffected, All their efforts at conversion ended in vain. (58)
lines: Having recited all the Koranic incantations,
The clerics failed to get the child converted.
As the true Khalsa (Subeg Singh's son) remained completely unaffected,
All their efforts at conversion ended in vain.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Nawab got exhausted after practising every torture, He could not see through the Guru's mysterious support of His Sikhs. Thereafter summoning both Subeg Singh and his son to his court, The Nawab ordered the discontinuation of every torture. (59)
lines: As the Nawab got exhausted after practising every torture,
He could not see through the Guru's mysterious support of His Sikhs.
Thereafter summoning both Subeg Singh and his son to his court,
The Nawab ordered the discontinuation of every torture.

blocks.text: The way both father and son were put behind the bars3 , Rattan Singh had narrated the account thoroughly. Since the Guru had upheld the dignity of Subeg Singh, His persecution has become a legend of supreme sacrifice. (60)
lines: The way both father and son were put behind the bars3 ,
Rattan Singh had narrated the account thoroughly.
Since the Guru had upheld the dignity of Subeg Singh,
His persecution has become a legend of supreme sacrifice.

blocks.text: Dohra:

It was in the year eighteen hundred two of Bikrami Samvat, (That the father son duo were persecuted by Lahore Nawab). This is how the legend of Subeg Singh's sacrifice occurred, Dear devout readers listen to its contents with faith and devotion. (61)
lines: It was in the year eighteen hundred two of Bikrami Samvat,
(That the father son duo were persecuted by Lahore Nawab).
This is how the legend of Subeg Singh's sacrifice occurred,
Dear devout readers listen to its contents with faith and devotion.

blocks.text: Chaupai Dohra Chaupai Dohra Chaupai The way I (the author) had heard this legend from my father, I (Rattan Singh) have narrated it in this episode. I have narrated the way in which I had heard it, Now (dear readers) listen to another new episode. (62)
lines: Chaupai Dohra Chaupai Dohra Chaupai The way I (the author) had heard this legend from my father,
I (Rattan Singh) have narrated it in this episode.
I have narrated the way in which I had heard it,
Now (dear readers) listen to another new episode.
